<image>
What is the histological classification of this kidney tissue sample?

A. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels
B. Normal renal
C. Red blood cells
D. Renal cancer

<think>The histological examination reveals large polygonal cells characterized by abundant, clear, vacuolated cytoplasm and distinct cell membranes. These cells possess centrally located nuclei and are separated by a delicate vascular network. This specific morphological pattern is the classic hallmark of clear cell renal cell carcinoma, effectively distinguishing the sample from normal renal tissue, stromal elements, or red blood cells.

The answer is D.</think><answer>D. Renal cancer</answer>

<image>
What is the tissue type of this renal biopsy image?

A. Red blood cells
B. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels
C. Renal cancer
D. Normal renal

<think>The image displays clusters of small, uniform epithelial cells characterized by round, basophilic nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm. These cells are arranged in structures consistent with renal tubules or glomerular tufts, separated by thin fibrous stroma. The architecture lacks the pleomorphism, mitotic activity, or disruption typically seen in renal cancer, supporting a diagnosis of normal renal tissue.

The answer is D.</think><answer>D. Normal renal</answer>

<image>
What is the tissue composition shown in this kidney image?

A. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels
B. Renal cancer
C. Red blood cells
D. Normal renal

<think>The image displays numerous large cells with abundant clear cytoplasm and centrally located nuclei, which are separated by a delicate vascular network. This specific morphological pattern is a hallmark characteristic of clear cell renal cell carcinoma, identifying the tissue composition as renal cancer.

The answer is B.</think><answer>B. Renal cancer</answer>

<image>
Classify this renal tissue image into the correct category.

A. Normal renal
B. Red blood cells
C. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels
D. Renal cancer

<think>The renal tissue exhibits prominent vacuolated clear cell morphology with distinct cell borders, arranged in nests separated by delicate fibrovascular septa. Although the cells appear relatively uniform without significant cytologic atypia or mitotic figures, this specific architectural pattern of clear cells within a fibrovascular network is a classic histological feature of clear cell renal cell carcinoma, distinguishing it from benign renal parenchyma.

The answer is D.</think><answer>D. Renal cancer</answer>

<image>
What renal tissue category does this image belong to?

A. Renal cancer
B. Red blood cells
C. Normal renal
D. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels

<think>The image displays a population of cells characterized by abundant, clear, vacuolated cytoplasm and distinct cell borders. These morphological features, combined with the presence of prominent nuclei, constitute the hallmark appearance of clear cell renal cell carcinoma. This specific cellular architecture distinguishes the tissue from normal renal parenchyma, isolated red blood cells, or stromal elements such as smooth muscle and fibrous tissue, thereby identifying the sample as renal cancer.

The answer is A.</think><answer>A. Renal cancer</answer>

<image>
What type of renal pathology is shown in this image?

A. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels
B. Normal renal
C. Renal cancer
D. Red blood cells

<think>The image displays nests of large polygonal cells with abundant, optically clear cytoplasm and distinct cell membranes. This morphological pattern is characteristic of clear cell renal cell carcinoma, where the clear appearance results from glycogen and lipid accumulation. These hallmark histological features identify the pathology as a type of renal cancer.

The answer is C.</think><answer>C. Renal cancer</answer>

<image>
What type of renal pathology is shown in this image?

A. Red blood cells
B. Renal cancer
C. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels
D. Normal renal

<think>The image displays dense, eosinophilic, wavy collagen bundles that are characteristic of fibrous stroma. This morphology lacks the distinct tubular or glomerular structures seen in normal renal parenchyma, as well as the cellular atypia associated with renal cancer or the presence of red blood cells. The observation of these specific stromal features, including smooth muscle and fibrous components, supports the identification of the tissue as stromal.

The answer is C.</think><answer>C. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels</answer>

<image>
What type of renal tissue is visible in this histopathology image?

A. Normal renal
B. Renal cancer
C. Stromal, including smooth muscle, fibrous stroma and blood vessels
D. Red blood cells

<think>The histopathology image reveals well-organized tubular structures lined by epithelial cells with uniform, basally located nuclei and abundant cytoplasm. This distinct tubular architecture is characteristic of normal renal tissue. The cellular arrangement lacks the disorganization, nuclear atypia, or mitotic figures associated with renal cancer, and it is not composed primarily of spindle cells, fibrous stroma, or red blood cells. Consequently, the observed morphology confirms the presence of normal renal tissue.

The answer is A.</think><answer>A. Normal renal</answer>
